title: Advanced Socio-Economic Engine
description: Replace the simple annual-feedback model with a richer multi-channel socio-economic engine (labour, productivity, education, housing, NHS, welfare, crime, long-term effects) supporting conservative/moderate/optimistic forecast modes and explicit uncertainty.
rationale: This is the leap from 'transparent toy' to 'credible model'. Realistic channels make scores and distributional analysis meaningful and underpin the research platform.
success_criteria: The simple feedback model is replaced behind the engine interface
All listed channels are modelled and documented with sources
Conservative/moderate/optimistic modes produce coherent, ordered outputs
Uncertainty is represented explicitly in outputs
Scoring consumes the new engine deterministically per mode
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Channels: labour participation, productivity, education, housing, NHS demand, welfare, crime, long-term economic effects, uncertainty modelling
- Forecast modes: conservative, moderate, optimistic

## Out of scope
- Distributional/by-group breakdowns (EPIC-013)
- Monte Carlo simulation tooling (EPIC-014)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-001 - replaces/extends the engine behind its interface
- EPIC-003 - new channels must feed scoring without breaking determinism
- EPIC-011 - slider metadata (effects/uncertainty) informs channel design

## Assumptions
- The engine exposes a swappable feedback strategy
- Channel relationships are documented, sourced and transparent
- Determinism preserved per forecast mode; uncertainty explicit

## Risks
- Complexity outruns transparency -> document every channel + source
- Spurious precision -> forecast ranges + uncertainty; clear caveats
- Breaking existing scores/tests -> introduce behind interface; re-baseline
- Calibration is contested -> cite assumptions; offer the three modes

## Future extensions
- Empirical calibration against historical data
- Region/cohort-specific channel parameters (feeds EPIC-013)
- Pluggable third-party economic modules
